title: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a colleague of Rabbi Zeira (II; see Zevachim 5a): "Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba were sitting, and Abaye sat beside them, and they sat and said — Abaye said to them," and in Ketubot 45b: "Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said, and some say Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba."

Hyman suggests that apparently he was a native of the Land of Israel and came to Babylonia with Rabbi Zeira in the time of Abaye, when all the traveling sages went down to Babylonia, and he taught Torah there in the academy, as we find in Bava Metzia 58a: "A tanna recited before Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba — he said to him, 'It is the other way round!'" and Menachot 17a: "A tanna recited before him — 'rather say,' etc."; and as cited in Seder Tannaim ve-Amoraim, wherever there is "before so-and-so" (as should be read), he was a sage in the academy. And since he was a native of the Land of Israel, he was therefore called by the title "Rabbi" — Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba.
He is mentioned in Moed Katan 12a, 12b, but Hyman calls this a scribal error and says it should read bar Avdimi, as cited there at 11a.

notes.text: Zevachim 5a directly places Zeira and Yitzchak bar Abba with Abaye. Hyman’s migration, academy and Rabbi-title arguments, his ZeiraII designation and the proposed Avdimi correction remain his account. The exact Seder Tannaim ve-Amoraim passage was not independently inspected.
